newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India seen awarding 400,000-600,000/T July diesel.
newsitem.headline: India seen awarding 400,000-600,000/T July diesel.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) is expected to award between 400,000 tonnes to 600,000 tonnes of high speed diesel for delivery in July, industry sources said on Wednesday.

IOC's tender to buy 40,000-45,000 tonne cargoes of 1.0-percent sulphur diesel for delivery to Madras or Haldia on the east coast and to Kandla on the west coast closed on Tuesday and is valid until May 29.
IOC bought an unexpectedly low 270,000 tonnes for June delivery compared to the 870,000 tonnes it awarded for May arrival cargoes.
Traders said a Middle East oil firm and two oil majors have submitted aggressive offers.

They said low offers into the west coast of India for 1.0 percent sulphur grade diesel were heard around $1.00 per barrel over Mideast quotes on a cost and freight (c-and-f) basis for deliveries in the first week of July.
For deliveries from the second to the fourth week of July, offers were at around $1.15-$1.35 per barrel over Mideast quotes c-and-f west coast.
Into the east coast of India, offers were quoted at between $1.90-$2.20 per barrel c-and-f basis.
Traders said Mideat related quotes for 0.5 percent sulphur diesel were about five-cents more.
On Mediterranean related basis, offers were around $14.50 per tonne premia into the west coast and at $21.80 per tonne premia for deliveries to the east coast.
Offers for 0.5 percent sulphur diesel were at $15.20 per tonne premia over Mediterranean quotes on a c-and-f basis to the west coast of India.
